newsitem.title: USA: King World not for sale, King says on CNBC.
newsitem.headline: King World not for sale, King says on CNBC.

text.p: King World Productions Inc chairman Roger King said on Tuesday that the company was not for sale.

"We were never on the block," he said in an interview on CNBC television. "We talked a couple of years back with a couple of companies about strategic alliances. Nothing ever went to the board." King did not provide details.
He said the company, a producer and distributor of television programming, was concentrating on increasing business by developing new talk programs and TV shows for children.
He said recent distribution renewal deals for its syndicated programs "Wheel of Fortune," and "Jeopardy" extended through the year 2002 would assure a steady stream of revenues.
He said the company was optimistic that talk show host Oprah Winfrey would decide within the next few months to extend the contract for King World to syndicate her popular TV talk program.
Last year, New World Communications Group Inc was widely rumored to have been in talks to buy King World. New World later was bought by News Corp Ltd.
Earlier on Tuesday, King World said its board declared a special dividend of $2 per common share and authorized a stock repurchase program for up to five million shares.
